source.title: Beyond Double Ascent via Recurrent Neural Tangent Kernel in Sequential Recommendation
source.authors: Rui-Hong Qiu; Zi-Liang Huang; Hongzhi Yin

record.tranche_reason: Tests model-size double ascent for recurrent networks in sequential recommendation, a new setting, using ranking metrics.
record.gate_note: Figure 4 reports test MRR@10 and NDCG@10 across widths for four datasets, separately for early stopping and end of training. Figure 1 summarizes the best performance per model and is not counted separately from the early-stopping results. Training loss and OverRec's comparison line do not measure the claimed test-error curve and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps RNN hidden width from 2 to 4096 on four sequential-recommendation datasets. It reports test MRR@10 and NDCG@10 at early stopping and at end of training (Fig. 4, Fig. 1). The authors describe a rise-fall-rise ('double ascent') curve. This is a model-wise double-descent test in a new setting (recommendation, ranking metrics).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors report that test ranking performance roughly ascends, descends, then ascends again as RNN width grows ('double ascent'), and they hypothesise it would continue toward infinite width. They then propose OverRec, an RNTK-based kNN method, which they claim approximates very wide RNNs and outperforms baselines.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a width sweep of trained recurrent models, widths 2 to 4096, on four sequential-recommendation datasets; reports ranking metrics rather than test error.
record.method_sensitivity: The width-sweep curves are reported separately for early-stopping and end-of-training performance.
record.problems: The width-sweep outcomes are presented in figures without tabulated numerical values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: The study does not locate the dip relative to the interpolation threshold. Training loss falls with width, but no width is identified as just fitting the training set. Only RNNs are tested, and widths stop at 4096, so how far the second ascent extends is unknown.
Fig. 1 and Fig. 4 colour points by epoch, but no epoch-wise test curve is analysed.
There is no sweep over training-set size.
There is no comparison across model classes. The RNTK/kNN method is the authors' own tool, not a capacity sweep.
There is no label-noise or regularization manipulation.
There is no re-parameterisation of complexity.

missing.what: Training cross-entropy loss versus width (Fig. 4, first column). This is needed to judge whether the test-performance dip sits near the width at which models fit the training set (V1's peak location). The record excludes it via gate_note, not rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: All V1 states rest on the authors' prose and the figures; no numeric values or uncertainty are given per width. Row states are kept as observed, but the 'roughly' qualifier and the per-dataset figure readings are unverified. Table II and Fig. 5-6 compare OverRec with baselines and are correctly excluded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests a width sweep for RNNs in sequential recommendation, not all deep-network architectures or other tasks.
No isolated test-performance curve over training epochs is reported.
No sweep over training-set size near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison across model classes to test a general double-descent curve.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location.
No test of label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No re-expression of the curve against an effective parameter count.

relationships.condition: RNN width sweeps (2 to 4096) on Beauty, Clothing, Toys and ML-1M; test MRR@10 and NDCG@10; early-stopping and end-of-training checkpoints
relationships.reason: Authors state the double ascent 'appears in both' checkpoint conditions across the four datasets (r1-r16). The evidence is figure-only, the authors say 'roughly', and the peak is not tied to the interpolation threshold.
relationships.display_finding: MRR@10 and NDCG@10 showed approximate double ascent across four datasets under early stopping and final checkpoints, without establishing alignment with interpolation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
